title: Contract anchors & edge cases — personal clipboard
content:
Purpose: quick personal clipboard for clauses I frequently flag or want to test during counterparty redlines. Not polished — shorthand + suggested caller lines so I don't flinch in review meetings.

Top-level anchors (quick read):
- Limit liability: target single-digit months of ARR / cap at $X (use formula: 3-6 months MRR for SMB; 12 months for enterprise) — pushback script: 'We can take commercial risk capped, but unlimited liability or broad consequential is a non-starter.'
- Indemnity: carveouts for customer misuse, downstream claims from outputs, and narrow to direct IP infringement only. Ask to flip broad customer indemnity to mutual for IP.
- IP & outputs: insist on customer ownership of customer data and outputs generated from that data; vendor retains model weights and pre-existing IP. Clarify training rights — no right to use customer PII to train models without explicit opt-in.
- Data residency & export: require explicit regions for storage/processing if customer regulated. If vendor supports multi-region, add SLA for region-by-region routing.
- Audit rights: limit frequency (e.g., once per 12 months), scope (security posture and logs, not full code/weights), and require HIPA/NDAs for auditors.
- Subprocessors / subcontractors: require 30-day notice and ability to object on reasonable security/regulatory grounds. Flow-down obligations for security and data handling.
- Security incidents: breach notification within 72 hours, include remediation plan and root cause summary; costs for mandatory notifications should be vendor's responsibility if breach due to vendor fault.
- SLA & remedies: define uptime target, measurement window, and service credit schedule. Avoid termination for SLA breaches unless repeated and severe.
- Termination & transition: confirm data return/erase timeline, transition assistance (X days at reduced rate), and escrow for critical artifacts if on-prem customer.
- Export controls & sanctions: vendor must comply and represent no export-restricted tech; ensure short stop-gap if sanctions block service (grace periods).

Clause-level heuristics (phrasing to search for / red-flag language):
- 'Unlimited liability' / 'not excluded by law' => flag immediately.
- 'Hold harmless to the fullest extent permitted by law' => ask to cap and narrow to direct damages.
- 'All data' / 'any output' used by vendor for training without consent => convert to 'Customer Data' only; require opt-in for training.
- 'Subcontractor may engage without notice' => require notice + objection right.
- 'Audits at vendor's discretion' => reverse so customer audit requires reasonable advance notice and scope limitations.
- 'Automatic renewals with no termination window' => require 60–90 day notice window for non-renewal.

Negotiation heuristics & scripts (one-liners to use live):
- When asked to accept broad indemnity: 'We're happy to indemnify for IP and proven vendor-caused losses; for all other categories let's align caps to the risk profile.'
- If vendor insists on training rights: 'We treat customer input as highly sensitive. We can consider aggregated, de-identified datasets with explicit DPA language — not raw customer content.'
- On SLA credits request: 'Credits are appropriate; termination should be reserved for material repeated failures, not isolated incidents.'

Walkaway / escalation triggers (my personal list):
- Vendor insists on unlimited liability for security/privacy events.
- Vendor claims rights to use raw customer content for model training without clear consent and controls.
- No reasonable data deletion or export mechanism within 30 days post-termination.
- Vendor refuses basic flow-downs to subprocessors for security/compliance needs.

Quick checklist for redline pass (checkbox shorthand I use):
- [ ] Liability cap in contract? number and formula documented.
- [ ] Indemnity scope mutual / IP-only?
- [ ] Outputs ownership & training rights clarified.
- [ ] Data residency clause present and scoped.
- [ ] Audit rights limited and governed.
- [ ] Subprocessor notice + flow-downs.
- [ ] Breach notification timing and responsibilities.
- [ ] Termination assistance + data return/erase window.
- [ ] SLA measurement & credit schedule included.
- [ ] Escrow or runway assurances for on-prem/private deployments (if applicable).

Notes / oddities I've seen recently (examples to reuse in review chats):
- Some vendors try to hide training rights inside 'analytics' definitions — call out and require explicit separation.
- For Dedicated vs Hosted: make sure SLAs map to the deployment model; dedicated should have stronger uptime/MTTR commitments.
- Customers often forget 'rate-limiting' language — add per-route throttles + priority tiers if product exposed to heavy traffic.

Templates/patterns I prefer to propose in counters:
- Liability cap: 'Aggregate liability shall not exceed the greater of $X or the fees paid in the preceding 12 months.'
- Indemnity: 'Each party shall indemnify the other for third-party claims alleging (i) IP infringement of the indemnifying party's technology, or (ii) gross negligence or willful misconduct.'
- Training use: 'Vendor shall not use Customer Data or Outputs to train models, perform model improvements, or derive weights, without Customer's prior written consent.'
- Subprocessor flow-down: 'Vendor shall ensure each subprocessor is bound by written obligations no less protective than those in this Agreement.'

Open questions I need to resolve before next legal sync:
- Preferred dollar value for liability caps at different account tiers (input from finance on acceptable exposure).
- Standard language for outputs ownership when customer is both uploading data and using vendor-hosted prompt templates.
- Escrow scope for private/on-premures — what exactly we require (config, DB schema, deployment scripts?).

End notes: keep this lightweight. Copy bits into counters depending on negotiation posture (commercial vs enterprise). Shuffle the walkaways if this is a strategic deal (tighten).

Recent changes/updates: added subprocessor objection window (30 days) and tightened training-rights language (Aug 2024).
